q: They shall stay thirty days for the righteous, sixty days for the sinners.

s: mourning for the dead lasts six months (for the righteous after death of the master or mistress of the house)
q: They shall stay six months for the righteous, a year for the sinners.

s: mourning for the dead lasts a year (for sinners after death of the master or mistress of the house)
q: They shall stay six months for the righteous, a year for the sinners.

s: mourning for the dead lasts twenty-five days (for the righteous after death of a grandparent or grandchild)
q: They shall stay twenty-five days for the righteous, fifty days for the sinners.

s: mourning for the dead lasts fifty days (for sinners after death of a grandparent or grandchild)
q: They shall stay twenty-five days for the righteous, fifty days for the sinners.

s: mourning for the dead lasts twenty days (for the righteous after death of an uncle or aunt)
q: They shall stay twenty days for the righteous, forty days for the sinners.

s: Ahura Mazda answers Zarathustra
q: Ahura Mazda answered: 'They shall stay thirty days for the righteous, sixty days for the sinners.'

s: mourning for the dead lasts forty days (for sinners after death of an uncle or aunt)
q: They shall stay twenty days for the righteous, forty days for the sinners.

s: mourning for the dead lasts fifteen days (for the righteous after death of a cousin)
q: They shall stay fifteen days for the righteous, thirty days for the sinners.

s: mourning for the dead lasts ten days (for the righteous after death of a cousin's child)
q: They shall stay ten days for the righteous, twenty days for the sinners.

s: mourning for the dead lasts five days (for the righteous after death of a cousin's grandchild)
q: They shall stay five days for the righteous, ten days for the sinners.

s: stranger is a person who does not profess the true faith or the true law
q: If a stranger dies who does not profess the true faith, or the true law

s: Ashemaogha is a wicked two-legged ruffian (ungodly)
q: that wicked, two-legged ruffian, that ungodly Ashemaogha

s: Ashemaogha defiles creatures of the good spirit (directly and indirectly while alive)
q: Whilst alive, indeed, O Spitama Zarathustra! that wicked, two-legged ruffian, that ungodly Ashemaogha, directly defiles the creatures of the good spirit, and indirectly defiles them.

s: Ashemaogha smite water (while alive)
q: Whilst alive he smites the water

s: Ashemaogha blow out Fire (while alive)
q: whilst alive he blows out the fire

s: house becomes clean after cleansing
q: then the house shall be clean

s: Ashemaogha carry off cow (while alive)
q: Whilst alive he carries off the cow

s: Ashemaogha smite faithful man (with a deadly blow while alive)
q: whilst alive he smites the faithful man with a deadly blow, that parts the soul from the body

s: Ashemaogha deprives faithful man (of food, clothing, house, bed, and vessels while alive)
q: Whilst alive, indeed, O Spitama Zarathustra! that wicked, two-legged ruffian, that ungodly Ashemaogha, never ceases depriving the faithful man of his food, of his clothing, of his house, of his bed, of his vessels

s: cleansing includes washing body (three times)
q: They shall wash their bodies three times

s: cleansing includes washing clothes (three times)
q: they shall wash their clothes three times

s: cleansing includes chanting Gâthas (three times)
q: they shall chant the Gâthas three times

s: cleansing includes sacrifice (offered to Fire)
q: they shall offer up a sacrifice to my Fire

s: cleansing includes offering baresma (bundles of baresma)
q: they shall offer up the bundles of baresma

s: cleansing includes libations (brought to good waters)
q: they shall bring libations to the good waters

s: dog Vanghâpara is a dog (with a prickly back and long, thin muzzle)
q: The dog with the prickly back, with the long and thin muzzle, the dog Vanghâpara, which evil-speaking people call the Duzaka; this is the good creature among the creatures of the good spirit

s: Vohunazga dog is a dog
q: either a shepherd's dog, or a house dog, or a Vohunazga dog, or a trained dog

s: trained dog is a dog
q: either a shepherd's dog, or a house dog, or a Vohunazga dog, or a trained dog

s: shepherd's dog guards fold (goes a Yugyêsti round about it, watching for the thief and the wolf)
q: It is the dog who goes a Yugyêsti round about the fold, watching for the thief and the wolf.

s: house dog guards house (goes a Hâthra round about it, watching for the thief and the wolf)
q: It is the dog who goes a Hâthra round about the house, watching for the thief and the wolf.

s: Vohunazga dog seeks subsistence (claims none of the talents of shepherd's or house dogs)
q: It is the dog who claims none of those talents, and only seeks for his subsistence.

s: young dogs is a dog
q: If a man shall smite a young dog so that it gives up the ghost and the soul parts from the body

s: dog is a good spirit (one of the creatures of the good spirit)
q: the dog, of all the creatures of the good spirit

s: dog eats milk and fat with meat (right food)
q: Bring ye unto him milk and fat with meat; this is the right food for the dog.

s: dog has characters eight different sorts of people
q: A dog has the characters of eight different sorts of people:--

s: dog Vanghâpara is a good spirit (good creature among its creatures)
q: The dog with the prickly back, with the long and thin muzzle, the dog Vanghâpara, which evil-speaking people call the Duzaka; this is the good creature among the creatures of the good spirit

s: dog has character priest (eats broken food, is grateful, easily satisfied, and wants only a small piece of bread)
q: He eats broken food, like a priest; he is grateful, like a priest; he is easily satisfied, like a priest; he wants only a small piece of bread, like a priest; in these things he is like unto a priest.

s: dog has character warrior (marches in front, fights for the beneficent cow, and goes first out of the house)
q: He marches in front, like a warrior; he fights for the beneficent cow, like a warrior; he goes first out of the house, like a warrior; in these things he is like unto a warrior.

s: dog has character husbandman (watchful, sleeps lightly, goes first out and returns last)
q: He is watchful and sleeps lightly, like a husbandman; he goes first out of the house, like a husbandman; he returns last into the house, like a husbandman; in these things he is like unto a husbandman.

s: dog has character strolling singer (sings, is intrusive, meagre, and poor)
q: He sings like a strolling singer; he is intrusive, like a strolling singer; he is meagre, like a strolling singer; he is poor, like a strolling singer; in these things he is like unto a strolling singer.

s: dog has character thief (likes darkness, prowls in darkness, is a shameless eater, and an unfaithful keeper)
q: He likes darkness, like a thief; he prowls about in darkness, like a thief; he is a shameless eater, like a thief;. he is an unfaithful keeper, like a thief; in these things he is like unto a thief

s: dog has character wild beast (likes darkness, prowls in darkness, is a shameless eater, and an unfaithful keeper)
q: He likes darkness, like a wild beast; he prowls about in darkness, like a wild beast; he is a shameless eater, like a wild beast; he is an unfaithful keeper, like a wild beast; in these things he is like unto a wild beast.

s: dog has character courtezan (sings, is intrusive, walks about the roads, meagre, and poor)
q: He sings, like a courtezan; he is intrusive, like a courtezan; he walks about the roads, like a courtezan; he is meagre, like a courtezan; he is poor, like a courtezan; in these things he is like unto a courtezan.

s: dog has character child (likes sleeping, apt to run away, full of tongue, and goes on all fours)
q: He likes sleeping, like a child; he is apt to run away, like a child; he is full of tongue, like a child; he goes on all fours, like a child; in these things he is like unto a child.

s: shepherd's dog belongs to Ahura Mazda (one of his two dogs)
q: If those two dogs of mine, the shepherd's dog and the house dog

s: house dog belongs to Ahura Mazda (one of his two dogs)
q: If those two dogs of mine, the shepherd's dog and the house dog

s: dog Vanghâpara kills evil spirit (from midnight till the sun is up, thousands of its creatures)
q: this is the good creature among the creatures of the good spirit that from midnight till the sun is up goes and kills thousands of the creatures of the evil spirit.

s: shepherd's dog supports house (together with the house dog, necessary for every house on earth)
q: For no house could subsist on the earth made by Ahura, but for those two dogs of mine, the shepherd's dog and the house dog.

s: house dog supports house (together with the shepherd's dog, necessary for every house on earth)
q: For no house could subsist on the earth made by Ahura, but for those two dogs of mine, the shepherd's dog and the house dog.

s: Ahura Mazda created dog (self-clothed and self-shod, watchful, wakeful, sharp-toothed, and born to take food from man and watch man's goods)
q: The dog, O Spitama Zarathustra! I, Ahura Mazda, have made self-clothed and self-shod, watchful, wakeful, and sharp-toothed, born to take his food from man and to watch over man's goods.

s: dog protects goods (when of sound mind, against the evil-doer)
q: I, Ahura Mazda, have made the dog strong of body against the evil-doer, and watchful over your goods, when he is of sound mind.

s: water dog is a dog (formed from the spring of the waters)
q: and there out of every thousand dogs and every thousand she-dogs, two water dogs are formed, a water dog and a water she-dog.

s: water she-dog is a dog (formed from the spring of the waters)
q: and there out of every thousand dogs and every thousand she-dogs, two water dogs are formed, a water dog and a water she-dog.

s: water dog causes drought (when killed; it dries up pastures)
q: He who kills a water dog brings about a drought that dries up pastures.

s: mad dog is a dog (bites without barking)
q: a mad dog, or one that bites without barking

s: scentless dog is a dog (scentless and in need of healing)
q: If there be in the house of a worshipper of Mazda a scentless dog, or a mad dog

s: wolf destroys fold (with dogs born of a he-dog and a she-wolf; more murderous, mischievous, and destructive than other wolves)
q: And there are born of a he-dog and of a she-wolf such wolves as fall on the shepherd's dog, on the house dog, on the Vohunazga dog, on the trained dog, and destroy the folds; such wolves are born as are more murderous, more mischievous, more destructive to the folds than any other wolves.

s: Duzaka is a dog Vanghâpara (name used by evil-speaking people)
q: The dog with the prickly back, with the long and thin muzzle, the dog Vanghâpara, which evil-speaking people call the Duzaka

s: sacrifice is offered to Sraosha (as atonement for killing dog Vanghâpara)
q: unless he has, while alive, atoned for his sin by offering up a sacrifice to Sraosha.

s: sacrifice is offered for water dog (for three days and three nights with fire blazing, baresma tied up, and Haoma uplifted)
q: until the murderer of the water dog has been smitten to death and the holy soul of the dog has been offered up a sacrifice, for three days and three nights with fire blazing, with baresma tied up, and with Haoma uplifted.

s: daêva Zairimyangura is a evil spirit (evil creature among its creatures)
q: The daêva Zairimyangura, which evil-speaking people call the Zairimyâka, this is the evil creature among the creatures of the evil spirit

s: daêva Zairimyangura kills good spirit (from midnight till the sun is up, thousands of its creatures)
q: this is the evil creature among the creatures of the evil spirit that from midnight till the sun is up goes and kills thousands of the creatures of the good spirit.

s: shepherd's dog is a dog
q: either a shepherd's dog, or a house dog, or a Vohunazga dog, or a trained dog

s: house dog is a dog
q: either a shepherd's dog, or a house dog, or a Vohunazga dog, or a trained dog

s: Fargard XIV. is a fargard
q: Fargard XIV.

s: penalty for killing a water dog includes soft wood (ten thousand loads brought to the fire of Ahura Mazda as atonement)
q: He shall godly and piously bring unto the fire of Ahura Mazda ten thousand loads of soft wood, of Urvâsna, Vohu-gaona, Vohu-kereti, Hadhâ-naêpata, or any sweet-scented plant, as an atonement unto the soul (of the water dog).

s: world of the wicked is entered by person who does not undergo the penalty for killing a water dog (with descent into the dark world made of darkness)
q: if he shall not undergo it, he shall fall down into the world of the wicked, into that dark world, made of darkness, the offspring of darkness.

s: penalty for killing a water dog includes baresma (ten thousand bundles tied and consecrated)
q: He shall godly and piously tie and consecrate ten thousand bundles of baresma

s: penalty for killing a water dog includes Zaothra libation (ten thousand offered to the good waters with Haoma and sacred meat)
q: he shall offer up to the good waters ten thousand Zaothra libations with the Haoma and the sacred meat

s: Zarathustra asks Ahura Mazda (about the penalty for killing a water dog)
q: Zarathustra asked Ahura Mazda: 'O Ahura Mazda, most beneficent Spirit, Maker of the material world, thou Holy One! He who smites one of those water dogs that are born one from a thousand dogs and a thousand she-dogs, so that he gives up the ghost and the soul parts from the body, what is the penalty that he shall pay?'

s: penalty for killing a water dog includes snakes (ten thousand that go upon the belly)
q: He shall kill ten thousand snakes of those that go upon the belly

s: penalty for killing a water dog includes tortoises (ten thousand)
q: he shall kill ten thousand tortoises

s: penalty for killing a water dog includes land frogs (ten thousand)
q: he shall kill ten thousand land frogs

s: penalty for killing a water dog includes water frogs (ten thousand)
q: he shall kill ten thousand water frogs

s: penalty for killing a water dog includes corn-carrying ants (ten thousand)
q: he shall kill ten thousand corn-carrying ants

s: penalty for killing a water dog includes biting ants (ten thousand that bite, dig holes, and work mischief)
q: he shall kill ten thousand ants of those that bite and dig holes and work mischief.

s: penalty for killing a water dog includes earth worms (ten thousand)
q: He shall kill ten thousand earth worms

s: penalty for killing a water dog includes horrid flies (ten thousand)
q: he shall kill ten thousand horrid flies.

s: penalty for killing a water dog includes holes for the unclean (ten thousand filled up)
q: He shall fill up ten thousand holes for the unclean.

s: Ahura Mazda is a Maker of the material world (most beneficent Spirit and Holy One)
q: Ahura Mazda: 'O Ahura Mazda, most beneficent Spirit, Maker of the material world, thou Holy One!

s: penalty for killing a water dog includes fire implements (twice seven sets given to godly men)
q: He shall godly and piously give to godly men twice seven sets of implements for the fire

s: water dog is a dog (born one from a thousand dogs and a thousand she-dogs)
q: one of those water dogs that are born one from a thousand dogs and a thousand she-dogs

s: water dog has soul of the water dog (when it gives up the ghost)
q: so that he gives up the ghost and the soul parts from the body

s: war implements include sacred girdle (eleventh)
q: the eleventh a girdle

s: water dog has body of the water dog
q: so that he gives up the ghost and the soul parts from the body

s: penalty for killing a water dog includes silver (one measure, valued at the price of a stallion)
q: one measure of silver and one measure of gold.' O Maker of the material world, thou Holy One! How much silver? Ahura Mazda answered: 'The price of a stallion:'

s: penalty for killing a water dog includes gold (one measure, valued at the price of a camel)
q: one measure of silver and one measure of gold.' O Maker of the material world, thou Holy One! How much silver? Ahura Mazda answered: 'The price of a stallion:' O Maker of the material world, thou Holy One! How much gold? Ahura Mazda answered: ‘The price of a camel.

s: penalty for killing a water dog includes ten thousand stripes (with the Aspahê-astra)
q: He shall pay ten thousand stripes with the Aspahê-astra, ten thousand stripes with the Sraoshô-karana.

s: penalty for killing a water dog includes rill of running water (procured for godly husbandmen)
q: He shall godly and piously procure a rill of running water for godly husbandmen

s: rill of running water has depth depth of a dog
q: The depth of a dog, and the breadth of a dog.

s: rill of running water has breadth breadth of a dog
q: The depth of a dog, and the breadth of a dog.

s: penalty for killing a water dog includes piece of arable land (given to godly men)
q: He shall godly and piously give a piece of arable land to godly men

s: piece of arable land is watered by rill of running water (on both sides)
q: As much as can be watered with such a rill on both sides.

s: penalty for killing a water dog includes house with ox-stalls (with nine hâthras and nine nematas)
q: He shall godly and piously procure for godly men a house with ox-stalls, with nine hâthras and nine nematas

s: house with ox-stalls has nine hâthras
q: a house with ox-stalls, with nine hâthras and nine nematas

s: house with ox-stalls has nine nematas
q: a house with ox-stalls, with nine hâthras and nine nematas
